session.name: handshake
session.note: a hello is answered with a version and a token

session.name: version-mismatch
session.note: a hello that shares no version gets no token

session.name: open-without-token
session.note: an open that carries no token is refused

session.name: open-wrong-token
session.note: an open with a token the host never issued is refused

session.name: token-single-use
session.note: a token opens once; the second open with it is refused and the first goes on

session.name: hello-replaces-token
session.note: a new hello invalidates the token of the previous one

session.name: open-busy
session.note: a second view cannot open while one is opening

session.name: bundle-partial
session.note: the host names only the digests it lacks, in manifest order

session.name: bundle-path-escape
session.note: a manifest path that leaves the bundle is refused

session.name: bye-needs-the-token
session.note: a bye ends the view only with the token that opened it; the open that is busy does not take that token's place

session.name: dismiss-and-reopen
session.note: a program closes its view without ending and opens one again: the closed answers its dismiss, and the second open finds the file in the store

session.name: dismiss-needs-the-token
session.note: a dismiss closes the view only with the token that opened it, not with the outstanding one; a token issued while the view was still opening is good once the view is gone

session.name: wasm-view
session.note: a host that shows WebAssembly views offers wasm, as the program listed it, asks for the component's file, hands the program's msg to the view without reading it, and a dismiss closes the view like any other

session.name: wasm-unsupported
session.note: a host that does not show WebAssembly views leaves wasm out of its welcome and refuses such an open as unsupported

session.name: no-common-version
session.note: a kind the host has no version of in common with the program is left out of the views of its welcome and named in its opens, with the versions the host does open, and an open of it is refused as unsupported; when no kind is left the welcome still carries a token

session.name: several-versions
session.note: the versions the host and the program share are listed in the program's order, not the host's; an open names one of them, and a version outside the list is refused as unsupported

session.name: manifest-before-limit
session.note: an open that is malformed and too big is refused as malformed: an entry of the wrong type, an access of the wrong shape, or an access that has an entry that is not a string past the bound of its list

session.name: access-limit
session.note: an access lists at most 32 origins in a list and 64 in all, valid or not; an open over a bound is refused as limit, and one at the bound goes on

session.name: screen-refused
session.note: a pane that is not on the alternate screen has its open refused as screen; once it is, the same program opens

session.name: policy-refused
session.note: a host whose own policy lets no program open a view answers a hello and refuses the open as policy

session.name: bundle-corrupt
session.note: a file whose bytes do not have the digest it is sent under ends the open as error bundle

session.name: bundle-files-ignored
session.note: a file nobody asked for and a file already verified for this open are ignored and stored nowhere; the view starts when the files asked for are all here

session.name: bundle-duplicate-digests
session.note: two files with the same bytes are one digest: the need names it once and one file message completes the bundle

session.name: files-timeout
session.note: an open whose files do not come in the time the host chose ends as error timeout

session.name: consent-timeout
session.note: an open that waits in vain for the answer of the person ends as error timeout, and the question is taken back

session.name: view-ends
session.note: the person closing a view and the view asking to close are told to the program as user and view, with no re because nothing of the program is outstanding; nothing the view says afterwards is written; a close is written after what the page said before it

session.name: page-message-too-long
session.note: a message of the page over 1 MiB ends the view as error view, since nobody could answer it; the message is not written

session.name: restart
session.note: a host that restarts a running view tears it down without a closed and offers a new token with restart; the program opens again with the new token and the old one is no more

session.name: messages-outside-a-view
session.note: a msg of the program reaches no view before one runs and none after it has closed; nothing of the view is written once it is over

session.name: hello-edges
session.note: a hello with no kind, or whose protocol versions are not a list of integers, is not answered; a kind listed twice counts once at its first place; an empty list of protocol versions shares none

session.name: kit-open-ignores-access
session.note: the access of an open of a view the host draws itself is not read: a broken one does not refuse the open and a good one asks the person nothing

session.name: bundle-limits
session.note: a manifest over a limit of the protocol is refused as limit: a file over 8 MiB, more than 64 MiB in all; one exactly at both limits goes on

session.name: bundle-too-many-files
session.note: a manifest of 1025 files is refused as limit: a bundle has at most 1024

session.name: context-resent
session.note: the page is told its context again when a member changes, and only then

session.name: view-backlog
session.note: a view whose words wait for the program up to 16 MiB goes on; asked about more, the host closes it as error view and holds nothing

session.name: attach-files
session.note: a program attaches two files to its lua 2.1 view: the host asks for both, keeps the one that is what its digest says and refuses the other in a second need, sends nothing for a file already attached, forgets one at detach, attaches it again from its store without asking for it, and refuses a file over 8 MiB for the limit

session.name: attach-without-files
session.note: an attach while no view runs, and one to a view opened at lua 2.0, which has no files beside its bundle, are answered with every digest refused for view

session.name: read-files
session.note: the person gives the view a file and the program reads it: two reads may be out and a third is busy; the terminal's bytes come back as data and its failure as data with the code; a handle nobody gave and a length over 1 MiB are refused; after a restart the handle is nothing and a late answer is dropped

session.name: save-files
session.note: the view asks for the Save panel and a second panel is dropped while it is open; the program writes the place the person chose to its end and is told wrote; a write at the wrong offset fails the file, which is thrown away, and later writes are ignored; a view that ends before the last write throws its file away; a write for a handle nobody gave is told handle

session.name: stage-files
session.note: the program takes the file the person gave through the host's folder: the host makes a pipe, names it, and says how far the file went; a stage the host cannot do is answered at once with why (a handle nobody gave, an offset past the end, a file that changed); a way that is gone is answered route and the program asks again from where it was; the program takes a stage back and is told cancelled; a third stage while two are out is busy, and what comes late is ignored

session.name: fetch-files
session.note: the program sends a file to the place the person chose through the host's folder: the host makes a pipe, names it and says when the file is saved; a way that is gone is answered route with the length the host holds, and the program sends the rest from there; a failure throws away what was written and fails the place, a fetch the program takes back throws it away and leaves the place as it was; a fetch at an offset that is not where the file stands, a place with its file done or failed, and a write to a place whose fetch is out are refused

session.name: stage-view-ends
session.note: a view that ends with a stage and a fetch out stops both, and throws away what the fetch wrote; what the terminal tells of them afterwards is ignored; the welcome that offers the view again has the folder too

session.name: stage-not-offered
session.note: a host that has no folder on the program's machine leaves stage out of its features, and a stage, a fetch or an unstage that comes all the same is ignored

session.name: stage-without-files
session.note: while no view runs there is no handle for a stage or a fetch to name: both are answered handle

bridge.note: the host's context for a page: every theme role, its selection and its palette, the terminal's font, the size of the pane, the person's language and time zone, the accessibility setting, and what the person allowed
the context of a host that knows only the background and the foreground of its theme: the other roles, the selection and the palette are made up, and what is not known is left out
a page that started listening late asks for the context again
the page asks to be closed
the page asks to open a link in the person's browser
a link that is not http or https is dropped
a call of the page goes to the program as it is
an object with more than one member is nobody's message of the host's: it goes to the program as it is
what is not an object is dropped
the program's answer goes to the page as it is
a message that is named like one of the host's own is dropped on its way to the page
a link of 8193 bytes is dropped; the limit is 8192
a link with a space in it is dropped: every byte is printable ASCII and not the space
a link with a character that is not ASCII is dropped
a call written over several lines: the line feeds go and the spaces stay, and the program is written the rest as it came
a call with text a frame cannot carry (a letter with an accent, a DEL, a character outside the first plane): the program is written the same message with each as an escape
a message nested 127 levels deep, the outermost object counting as the first, is a message: it goes to the program as it is
a message nested 128 levels deep is none: it is dropped
the same, from the program: 127 levels go to the page as they are
the same, from the program: 128 levels are dropped
a link of exactly 8192 bytes is put to the person

message.note: the greatest id a message may have, 2^53 - 1
an id over 2^53 - 1 is no id: the message is ignored
a number whose value is a whole number is an id, whatever its form: 1.0 is 1
an id with a fraction is none
a string is not an id
a call nested 127 levels deep, the outermost object counting as the first, is read
a call nested 128 levels deep is no message: it is ignored
